terra.problem: This is a flat restatement of the verse, with little of Papa Dorin's personality.
The text says Gideon squeezed the fleece the next morning, not that he had planned to do so.
Saying God wanted no doubt goes beyond His stated reason: preventing Israel from glorifying themselves over Him.
The text does not say the men who turned back all had the same thought.
The explanation is generic and ends with a flat observation about the group's size.
This repeats the count and summarizes it without much of Papa Dorin's voice.

The claim that the men are staying home and nobody gets called back goes beyond the text. Later, men from Naphtali, Asher and Manasseh are called out, though the text does not identify them as the same individuals.
Nobody guessed that is an unsupported claim about what people guessed.
The clear forecast and absence of a storm assert weather conditions the text does not give. It only says the interpretation was not about a storm.
The text does not say that nobody in the valley could see anything coming.
The explanation repeats the same point several times without adding much personality or insight.

The text says the LORD set all the men in the camp against one another. The camp also included Amalekites and other people of the east, so describing the fight as among the Midianites themselves narrows the text.
Gideon tells the men to seize the waters ahead of the Midianites, and the text says they captured the waters. It does not explicitly say whether they got there ahead of them.
The text does not say the men pursued the Midianites all the way across the Jordan or that Gideon was waiting there.
The passage says Gideon was on the other side of the Jordan, but does not say he was still in the thick of the pursuit.
